title: Counterdiabatic quasi-Floquet control for the generation of entangled BICs using giant atoms
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Pedro Orellana, Ariel Norambuena
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) provide a mechanism for preserving entanglement in waveguide quantum electrodynamics. Here, using quantum control techniques in a configuration of two braided giant atoms, we propose a robust approach to create high-fidelity entangled BICs. The protocol combines quasi-Floquet modulation of the effective atom--waveguide couplings with an independent phase-controlled atomic exchange, which provides restricted counterdiabatic assistance for preparing the complete dressed BIC. In the lossless effective model, we obtain a full-state BIC fidelity of $0.99992$ and an unconditional atomic Bell fidelity of $0.99588$ using a fast control protocol. Microscopic finite-mode simulations validate the central-sideband description during the passage, while static calibration-error scans quantify its control tolerances. A separate microscopic study with relaxation and dephasing, using experimentally motivated component scales, identifies a finite useful entanglement window and a benefit from shaping the coupling envelopes. These results support controlled preparation, retention, and retrieval of dressed entanglement within the stated control and noise assumptions.
summary: This paper proposes a quantum control scheme to generate and preserve entangled Bound States in the Continuum (BICs) using two giant atoms coupled to a waveguide. By implementing a combination of quasi-Floquet modulation and counterdiabatic driving, the authors achieve near-perfect fidelity in preparing the entangled state. This demonstrates a powerful method for controlling quantum information storage in engineered photonic environments.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of generating and maintaining high-fidelity entanglement within Bound States in the Continuum (BICs) using giant atoms coupled to a waveguide.
main_result: A robust protocol combining quasi-Floquet modulation and phase-controlled atomic exchange achieves high-fidelity entanglement, reaching a full-state BIC fidelity of 0.99992 in the lossless limit.
method: The approach utilizes quantum control techniques, specifically quasi-Floquet modulation and state-selective counterdiabatic driving, applied to the effective Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system consists of two giant atoms coupled to a one-dimensional coupled-resonator waveguide. The dynamics are modeled using an effective slow-frame Hamiltonian derived from the full time-dependent Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Full-state BIC fidelity (0.99992), unconditional atomic Bell fidelity (0.99588), Concurrence, and state-selective tracking residuals.
important_parameters: The control is governed by modulation envelopes $ eta_i(t)$ and the coupling strengths $g_{ik}$, with performance quantified under specific control tolerances.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the central sideband approximation, and the derivation of the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian requires assumptions about the initial state and the nature of the control fields.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the physical system, the state-preparation protocol (involving a $\pi$-pulse and CD exchange), and the temporal control sequence applied to the system.
paper_structure: The paper develops the effective Hamiltonian, derives the necessary counterdiabatic control Hamiltonian, outlines a two-stage preparation protocol (including $\pi$-pulse and coupling variation), and validates the results using both lossless and dissipative simulations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines advanced quantum control theory (Floquet engineering, counterdiabatic driving) with a physical platform (giant atoms/waveguides) known for studying open quantum systems and engineered photonic states.
